byte_form_policy: each hash below is the sha256 of the file bytes in the final deliverable tree (the audited mission worktree in its gitattributes-normalized state, Windows, core.autocrlf=true): pre-existing tracked auto-text files render CRLF on this platform (OPEN_ITEMS.md, calibration/daily_scoreboard.py, tests/test_calibration_daily_scoreboard.py, legacy_differential_result.json); files authored LF in this mission chain carry their LF bytes, for which the byte hash EQUALS the git-canonical staged-blob sha256 (the two mission-authorization contracts, july13 packet, compare_legacy_differential.py); governance/artifacts/universal_connected_path_graph.json is .gitattributes-pinned text eol=lf, so its only package form is LF under EVERY measurement — a transient CRLF copy in a writer's worktree is never package content (git normalizes it on stage/apply), which is exactly the defect the correction_history entry records
verification_procedure: git worktree add --detach <dir> a0d5e3b9a5f9731357465f93fe2375f9a4672338; cd <dir>; git apply --check <lane_a.patch>; git apply --index <lane_a.patch>; then EVERY entry below must equal the fresh-apply worktree byte sha256 OR the git-canonical staged blob sha256 ('git cat-file blob :<path>' | sha256) — the graph entry must equal BOTH
procedure_variance_disclosure: on core.autocrlf=true platforms 'git apply' (with or without --index) smudges NEWLY-ADDED auto-text files to CRLF in the working tree, so the 4 LF-authored entries verify against their staged-blob hashes (== the recorded values) rather than the smudged worktree rendering; the 4 CRLF-rendered entries verify against worktree bytes (their LF blob forms differ and are NOT the recorded convention); this split is disclosed rather than silently convention-switched because the CRLF renderings are what the audited platform materializes for pre-existing files and the recorded values are what Cursor's digest audit confirmed
